chunks.arabic_text: ٥ - سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، النَّخَعِيُّ، أَبُو دَاوُدَ، يُقَالُ لَهُ: كَاذِبُ النَّخَعِ.

translations.en: 5 – Sulaymān b. Hārūn, al-Nakhʿī, Abū Dāwud, it is said about him: the liar of al-Nakhʿ.

chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).

en.summary: Sulayman ibn Harun al-Nakh'i, a contemporary of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), is cited in al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* as a 'very weak' narrator, earning the specific epithet 'the liar of al-Nakh' for his propensity for errors or fabrication. This designation highlights the rigorous scrutiny applied to individual narrators within the Shia tradition, distinguishing between general weakness and specific tendencies toward untruthfulness in the chain of transmission.
en.seo_question: Who is Sulayman ibn Harun al-Nakh'i and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ هَارُونَ: Sulayman ibn Harun, the narrator being evaluated
key_terms.النَّخَعِيُّ: Al-Nakh'i, a nisba indicating origin from the tribe of Nakh' or a place named Nakh'
key_terms.أَبُو دَاوُدَ: Abu Dawud, the kunya (patronymic) of the narrator
key_terms.كَاذِبُ النَّخَعِ: The liar of al-Nakh', a specific epithet used to describe his tendency to err or fabricate
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا: Very weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator with low reliability
